clue.text: Available current needed for going into production

parts.note: something available or operating is on
a stream is a current of water

explanation.surface: A factory needs electricity before it can start making things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Available current' reads as electricity on tap, but it splits into two pieces; 'needed for' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that is coming on stream is starting up and beginning to produce output.

clue.text: Scores for musical items in church? Just the reverse

indicators.note: the clue first says musical items go in church, then tells us to swap that round so church goes inside the musical items

parts.note: notes are the items of a piece of music

explanation.surface: A question about music scores used in church, with a twist.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' of the surface is a decoy: 'Just the reverse' tells you to turn the container round, so church goes inside the musical items.
explanation.definitionFit: Scores are tally marks cut into wood, the same thing as small nicks kept as a count.

clue.text: Giving, an impression of imminent flight

explanation.surface: Someone appears to be about to take wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving an impression of someone means mimicking them, and an aircraft about to leave the runway is on the point of becoming airborne.

clue.text: Why, say, soil on top is uncultivated

indicators.note: in a down entry the soil piece sits on top of the letter

parts.note: soil is earth

indicators.note: say signals that the word why is to be taken by its sound, a single letter

parts.note: the word why sounds like the letter Y

explanation.surface: Asking why some land has topsoil but has never been farmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncultivated' looks like a farming word to go with soil, but it means coarse or unrefined.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is crude and unrefined, lacking polish or culture.

clue.text: A grim era dispelled with liberty under Union Charter

indicators.note: in a down entry the liberty piece goes below the rearranged letters
dispelled means scattered, so the letters of a grim era are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: licence is liberty or freedom to act

explanation.surface: A dark period ends with freedom granted under a union's founding document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union or a political union; here it is the union of two people in wedlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding needs an official document permitting the union, a charter of sorts for the couple.

clue.text: Youngster is married in art school

parts.note: a cub is a youngster, a young animal or young scout

explanation.surface: A young person marries while at art college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art school' looks like a college; it is a movement in painting.
explanation.definitionFit: The movement of Picasso and Braque is a school of painting, a style shared by a group of artists.

clue.text: Insurance restriction is removed before retirement

parts.note: insurance gives cover
a let is an obstruction or restriction, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: An insurance policy loses a limitation clause before someone retires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests leaving work; here it is going to bed, and 'is' links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedspread is taken off the bed before you climb in for the night.

clue.text: One Isolde moved to love

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: moved means shifted about, so the letters of Isolde are rearranged

explanation.surface: Isolde, of Tristan and Isolde, is stirred to love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' looks emotional, to go with the lover from Wagner's opera, but it is the anagram signal on the name.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship someone is to love them to excess, adoring them like a god.

clue.text: A Christmas hangover suffered by the host

definitions.text: A Christmas hangover suffered by the host

parts.words: A Christmas hangover suffered by the host
parts.note: not the morning after a party: a seasonal plant hung over doorways, living as a parasite on a host tree

explanation.surface: The party-giver wakes up with a headache after Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hangover' is something that hangs over, and 'host' is the tree a parasitic plant feeds on.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasitic evergreen with white berries, hung up at Christmas, grows on host trees such as apple.

clue.text: Crew man showing little variation in stroke

indicators.note: a small variation of the letters of stroke, rearranging them only slightly

explanation.surface: A rower whose stroke barely changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crew man' and 'stroke' suggest rowing; the man stokes a ship's furnace, and only the R of STROKE moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's crew includes the man who shovels coal into the boilers.

clue.text: Starving birds circling centre of harbourage

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the birds are placed around the letters picked out

parts.note: ravens are birds

indicators.note: the centre of the word harbourage is its middle two letters

explanation.surface: Hungry birds wheel over a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The word harbourage has ten letters, so its centre is a pair of letters rather than one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone starving is extremely hungry, ready to devour anything.

clue.text: Collect for service in China

explanation.surface: Picking someone up for a job in China.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap a man to serve as a sailor was a practice named after a port; it is also a great city on China's coast.

clue.text: Renew the charge -. arbitrator indisposed

parts.note: a referee, ref for short, is an arbitrator
indisposed means ill

explanation.surface: A sick referee renews an accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' reads as an accusation, but it is a fresh load, as of a pen or a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: To top up a glass or pen again is to renew its contents.

clue.text: Race meeting for :a: northerner

parts.note: a Scot comes from the north of Britain

explanation.surface: A northerner goes to the races.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a famous English racecourse whose June meeting is a society event.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Ascot is a summer horse-racing event in Berkshire.

clue.text: Reliance upon delivery carrying our Times

indicators.note: in a down entry the delivery piece carries the other on its top

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks our era
diction is a speaker's manner of delivery

explanation.surface: Depending on a delivery van to bring this newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our Times' slyly names the newspaper; here it is the present era, AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Dependence on a drug or habit is a craving one cannot do without.

clue.text: Contract for a concert

explanation.surface: Signing a deal to perform a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a binding deal, and acting in concert means acting in accord.

clue.text: Small fellow ready to fight for America

parts.note: minute means tiny
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A little man eager to fight for the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The Minutemen were colonial militia in the American Revolution, ready to turn out at a minute's notice.
explanation.definitionFit: American colonial militiamen pledged to take up arms at a moment's warning.

clue.text: Shortage of transport in southern metropolis

indicators.note: in places the transport piece inside the other pieces

parts.note: a metropolis is a city
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A southern city lacks enough transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack or dearth of something means there is too little of it.

clue.text: Liable to tax provided in notes — one denomination

indicators.note: in places the provided piece between the two notes

parts.note: D and F are two musical notes
if means provided that
the Roman numeral I is one
a cult is a religious denomination or sect

explanation.surface: Something taxable in banknotes of one denomination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax' and 'denomination' suggest money; here tax means strain, and a denomination is a religious group.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taxing strains the solver's powers, hard to manage.

clue.text: Start of festival. — not just amusements

definitions.note: a plural word for a collection of rides and stalls, which is one thing

indicators.note: the start of the word festival is its first letter

parts.note: not just means unfair

explanation.surface: The festival opens, and not only with entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not just' reads as 'not only', but it means not fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling show of rides and sideshows offers amusements.

clue.text: Spiteful Enid's conversion

indicators.note: conversion means changing form, so the letters of Enid's are rearranged

explanation.surface: Enid has turned nasty, or found religion.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Enid's' is used as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneering, malicious remark is spiteful in tone.

clue.text: Working in daylight boy climbs round weird ruin

indicators.note: round means placed around, so the turned-up boy goes about the other letters
in a down entry climbing means reading upwards, so the boy is reversed

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: weird means strange, so the letters of ruin are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy scrambles over a strange ruin in daylight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbs' turns the boy upward to DAL, and 'round' puts that around IURN, the anagram from 'weird'.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals active by day rather than night are daytime creatures.

clue.text: At home, depression set in

parts.note: someone at home is in
a dent is a hollow or depression

explanation.surface: Gloom took hold while someone was at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression set in' reads as gloom arriving, but depression is a hollow and 'set in' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin a line further from the margin is to set its start inward, as typists do.

clue.text: Cato, perhaps, sounds like a swinger

indicators.note: sounds like says that a word for a swinger is to be heard rather than spelled

parts.note: a censer is the vessel of incense swung in church

explanation.surface: A Roman statesman is said to resemble a playboy.
explanation.walkthrough: Cato the Elder held the Roman office that supervised public morals, earning the nickname 'the Censor'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato was a Roman magistrate who kept the census and policed morals, an example of the office.

clue.text: Provide version of prisoner's right

parts.note: a con is a prisoner, and the possessive gives the S
true means right or correct

explanation.surface: Offer an account of a convict's rights.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret a text is to give your reading or translation of it.

clue.text: Reported to be fighting idleness

explanation.surface: Accounts say the soldiers were in combat, or just doing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reported to be fighting' is said of troops described as engaged in battle; spoken, that two-word phrase is identical to the one word for idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing nothing at all is a state of idleness.

clue.text: Hesitant claim to fur

parts.note: er is a hesitant sound
saying mine is laying claim to something

explanation.surface: Someone shyly claims a fur coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The white winter coat of the stoat is a prized pelt used on robes.

clue.text: Soldiers in the northern approaches in Europe

indicators.note: in puts the soldiers piece inside the other pieces

parts.note: a way is an approach or route
OR, other ranks, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are stationed in the northern approaches of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scandinavian kingdom is a country found in Europe.

clue.text: Tie up damaged net to fish

indicators.note: a damaged thing is broken up, so the letters of net are rearranged

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Knot up a torn net before fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges NET into ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To snarl or twist things together is to tie them up in knots.
